column1: In early April 2019, Dr Ceri Shipton and his colleagues from Australian National University became the first archaeologists to explore Obi, one of many tropical islands in Indonesia’s Maluku Utara province.
column2: 2019年4月初，澳大利亚国立大学的塞里·希普顿博士和同事们成为首批考察奥比岛的考古学家。奥比岛是印度尼西亚北马鲁古省众多热带岛屿中的一个。

column1: The research team’s discoveries suggest that the prehistoric people who lived on Obi were adept on both land and sea, hunting in the dense rainforest, foraging on the seashore, and possibly even voyaging between islands.
column2: 团队的发现表明，史前奥比岛人既擅长陆上活动，也善于在海上谋生：他们在密林里狩猎，在海边采集食物，甚至有可能在岛屿之间航行。

column1: The excavations were part of a project to learn more about how people first dispersed from mainland Asia, through the Indonesian archipelago and into the prehistoric continent that once connected Australia and New Guinea.
column2: 这次发掘属于一个研究项目，旨在进一步了解早期人类最初如何从亚洲大陆迁徙，穿过印度尼西亚群岛，到达一个在史前曾将澳大利亚和新几内亚连为一体的大陆。

column1: The team’s earlier research suggested that the northernmost islands in the group, known as the Wallacean islands, including Obi, would have offered the easiest migration route.
column2: 研究团队此前的研究表明，群岛最北端的那些岛屿（包括奥比岛在内的华莱西亚群岛）很可能曾为迁徙提供最便捷的路线。
column7: would have offered|很可能曾提供

column1: It also seemed likely that these islands were crucial ‘stepping stones’ on humans’ island-hopping voyages through this region millennia ago.
column2: 它们似乎很可能是数千年前人类在这个地区逐岛航行时至关重要的“落脚点”。

column1: But to support this idea, they needed archaeological evidence for humans living in this remote area in the ancient past.
column2: 不过，要支持这一设想，他们需要找到考古证据，证明在远古时期曾有人类生活在这片偏远地区。
column3: support this idea|支持这一设想
column6: in the ancient past|在远古时期

column1: So, they travelled to Obi to look for sites that might reveal evidence of early occupation.
column2: 于是，他们前往奥比岛，寻找可能留有早期人类居住证据的遗址。

column1: Just inland from the village of Kelo on Obi’s northern coast, Shipton and his colleagues found two caves containing prehistoric rock shelters that were suitable for excavation.
column2: 在奥比岛北海岸的凯洛村稍往内陆的地方，希普顿和同事发现了两个洞穴，内有适合发掘的史前岩棚遗址。
column6: prehistoric rock shelters|史前岩棚遗址

column1: With the permission and help of the local people of Kelo, they dug a small test excavation in each shelter.
column2: 征得凯洛当地居民同意并得到他们的帮助后，研究人员在每个岩棚内都做了一次小规模试掘。

column1: There they found numerous artefacts, including fragments of axes, some dating to about 14,000 years ago.
column2: 他们在那里发现了大量人工制品，其中包括斧头碎片，有些可追溯到约1.4万年前。

column1: The earliest axes at Kelo were made using clam shells.
column2: 凯洛最早的斧头是用蛤壳制成的。

column1: Axes made from clam shells from roughly the same time had also previously been found elsewhere in this region, including on the nearby island of Gebe to the northeast.
column2: 此前，在该地区的其他地方也发现过大致属于同一时期的蛤壳斧，其中包括东北方向不远处的格贝岛。
column4: roughly the same time|大致相同的时期

column1: As on Gebe, it is highly likely that Obi’s axes were used in the construction of canoes, thus allowing these early peoples to maintain connections between communities on neighbouring islands.
column2: 与格贝岛上的情况一样，奥比岛的斧头很可能也用于建造独木舟，使早期居民得以维持相邻岛屿各社群之间的联系。

column1: The oldest cultural layers from the Kelo site provided the team with the earliest record for human occupation on Obi, dating back around 18,000 years.
column2: 凯洛遗址最古老的文化层为团队提供了奥比岛上最早的人类居住记录，可追溯到约1.8万年前。

column1: At this time the climate was drier and colder than today, and the island’s dense rainforests would likely have been much less impenetrable than they are now.
column2: 当时气候比今天更干燥、更寒冷，岛上的密林很可能也远没有现在这么难以穿越。
column3: drier and colder|更干燥、更寒冷

column1: Sea levels were about 120 metres lower, meaning Obi was a much larger island, encompassing what is today the separate island of Bisa, as well as several other small islands nearby.
column2: 当时海平面要低大约120米，也就是说，奥比岛比现在大得多：如今已独立成岛的比萨岛及附近另外几个小岛，当时也在它的范围内。

column1: Roughly 11,700 years ago, as the most recent ice age ended, the climate became significantly warmer and wetter, no doubt making Obi’s jungle much thicker.
column2: 约1.17万年前，随着最近一次冰期结束，气候明显变暖、变湿，奥比岛的丛林无疑也因此变得更加茂密。
column6: warmer and wetter|更温暖、更湿润

column1: According to the researchers, it is no coincidence that around this time the first axes crafted from stone rather than sea shells appear, likely in response to their heavy-duty use for clearing and modification of the increasingly dense rainforest.
column2: 研究人员认为，恰在这一时期，第一批以石头而非海贝壳制成的斧头出现了，这并非巧合。这很可能是因为人们需要用斧头从事清理、改造日益茂密的雨林等重活。

column1: While stone takes about twice as long to grind into an axe compared to shell, the harder material keeps its sharp edge for longer.
column2: 用石头磨出一把斧头所花的时间大约是用贝壳的两倍，但石头更硬，斧刃也能更长时间保持锋利。

column1: Judging by the bones which the researchers unearthed in the Kelo caves, people living there mainly hunted the Rothschild’s cuscus, a possum-like creature that still lives on Obi today.
column2: 从研究人员在凯洛洞穴出土的骨骼判断，当地人主要猎捕罗氏袋貂。这种动物外形像袋貂，今天仍生活在奥比岛上。

column1: As the forest grew more dense, people probably used axes to clear patches of forest and make hunting easier.
column2: 随着森林变得更加茂密，人们很可能用斧头清出一块块林地，使狩猎变得容易些。
column3: grew more dense|变得更加茂密

column1: Shipton’s team’s excavation of the shelters at the Kelo site unearthed a volcanic glass substance called obsidian, which must have been brought over from another island, as there is no known source on Obi.
column2: 希普顿团队在发掘凯洛遗址的岩棚时，出土了一种名叫黑曜石的火山玻璃。由于奥比岛上没有已知产地，这种材料必定是从另一个岛上带来的。
column8: must have been brought|一定是被带来的
column9: no known source|没有已知产地

column1: It also revealed particular types of beads, similar to those previously found on islands in southern Wallacea.
column2: 发掘中还发现了一些特定类型的珠子，与先前在华莱西亚地区南部岛屿上发现的珠子相似。

column1: These finds again support the idea that Obi islanders routinely travelled to other islands.
column2: 这些发现再次支持了这样的看法：奥比岛居民经常前往其他岛屿。
column4: support the idea|支持这一看法

column1: The excavations suggest people successfully lived in the two Kelo shelters for about 10,000 years.
column2: 发掘结果表明，人们曾在凯洛的这两个岩棚中顺利生活了约一万年。
column7: for about 10,000 years|持续约一万年

column1: But then, about 8,000 years ago, both were abandoned.
column2: 可是大约8000年前，这两个岩棚都被人们弃用了。

column1: Did the residents leave Obi completely, or move elsewhere on the island?
column2: 居民是彻底离开了奥比岛，还是搬到了岛上的其他地方？

column1: Perhaps the jungle had grown so thick that axes were no longer a match for the dense undergrowth.
column2: 也许丛林已经变得极为茂密，以至于人们仅靠斧头已对付不了浓密的林下植被。
column5: no longer a match for|再也应付不了

column1: Perhaps people simply moved to the coast and turned to fishing rather than hunting as a means of survival.
column2: 也许人们只是搬到了海边，不再以打猎为生，而是转向了捕鱼。
column7: a means of survival|谋生手段

column1: Whatever the reason for the departure, there is no evidence for use of the Kelo shelters after this time, until about 1,000 years ago, when they were re-occupied by people who owned pottery as well as items made out of gold and silver.
column2: 不论他们为何离开，此后都找不到人们使用凯洛岩棚的证据。直到大约1000年前，拥有陶器以及金银制品的人们才重新来到岩棚居住。
column3: Whatever the reason|不论原因为何

column1: It seems likely, in view of Obi’s location, that this final phase of occupation also saw the Kelo shelters used by people involved in the historic trade in spices between the Maluku islands and the rest of the world.
column2: 鉴于奥比岛的地理位置，在最后这段有人居住的时期，凯洛岩棚很可能也曾由这样一些人使用：他们参与了当时马鲁古群岛与世界其他地区之间的香料贸易。
column9: the rest of the world|世界其他地区
